ideas.title: Stack Until It Falls (1 → 1,000)
ideas.hook: Frame 1: a glowing block is already falling onto a thin neon platform, with a counter at '1' in yellow.
ideas.why: 3D Zone's '%1,000,000 Satisfying iPhone Stacking Video' is at 3,644,337 views (4.4x its average, 6 days old), and the R&D Lab lists it as a format lead. It has the same wait-for-the-end payoff as your best Shorts (pendulum wave 31,776 views at 94% watched; brick breaker 9,322 at 99.5%): one system building toward an obvious end. No stacking format exists in sims.py yet.
ideas.script:
New sims.py function stack_collapse(). Objects: plain rounded rectangles 'blocks' (no logos, no phone shapes), 140x40 px, dropped one at a time from y=260 onto a 360 px platform centred at y=1380. Physics: 2D rigid bodies (pymunk), gravity 1800 px/s², friction 0.7, elasticity 0.05; each new block spawns with a random x offset ±18 px and drop interval that shrinks from 0.45 s to 0.08 s so the counter speeds up (1, 2, 5, 10, 25, 50, 100...). Win/ending: the tower leans and collapses at ~16 s; slow-mo 0.4x for the fall, then the counter freezes and flashes. Looping end: the last 0.5 s fades the debris out and a single block falls again onto the empty platform, matching frame 1. Colours on near-black #07070c: blocks cycle cyan #22e4ff → magenta #ff3fd8 → lime #9dff3a → orange #ff9a1f with a soft glow; platform white 60%. On-screen lines (y=150-330): white 'How high before it falls?' then yellow counter 'x 1' growing; at collapse yellow 'It fell at <N>!'. Sound: a soft wood-tick per landing pitched up as the stack grows (C major pentatonic), a low rumble + crash at collapse. Length 20 s.
Description: How many blocks can one tower hold? Watch until it falls. 🧱
Hashtags: #shorts #satisfying #physics #simulation #stacking
Tags: stacking simulation, satisfying physics, tower collapse, block stacking, physics simulation, satisfying video, oddly satisfying, bounce theory, simulation shorts, wait for it

ideas.title: Soft Body 0% vs 100% Escape
ideas.hook: Frame 1: three glowing jelly blobs (0%, 50%, 100% soft) already falling into three stacked spinning rings, each with a small gap.
ideas.why: ArtikAnimates' 'Verity 0% vs 100% Soft Body Simulation' is at 3.5M views (37x its average) and MORPHIK 3D's cloth sim at 3.46M (44x). Bounce Theory has no deformable-body format yet; the escape mechanic is already proven on your channel (6 colors, only 1 stays inside: 683 views).
ideas.script:
New sims.py function softbody_escape(). Objects: 3 lanes stacked vertically (centres y≈420, 860, 1300; rings radius 170, line width 8, gap 40°, each spinning 0.9 rad/s, alternating direction). In each ring one soft blob = 24-node spring-mass ring around a pressure centre (radius 38), spring stiffness 1.0 / 0.35 / 0.08 for 0% / 50% / 100% soft, damping 0.02, gravity 1400 px/s², restitution 0.85. Rigid 0% blob bounces cleanly; 100% blob splats, wobbles and squeezes through the gap. Win: first blob whose centre leaves its ring gets a burst of 40 particles + 'ESCAPED' tag; keep running until all 3 escape or 25 s; ranking shown 1st/2nd/3rd. Looping ending: final frame fades the escaped blobs back to their start positions (last 0.6 s cross-fade to frame 1). Colours on near-black #07070c: 0% cyan #22e4ff, 50% magenta #ff3fd8, 100% lime #9dff3a, ring glow white 40%. On-screen lines (white, y=150-330): 'Which one escapes first?' then yellow 'Hard vs Soft vs Jelly 😳'; small labels '0% SOFT', '50% SOFT', '100% SOFT' left of each ring. Sound: rigid hits = short marimba pluck (pitch by speed), soft hits = low squish (filtered noise burst + pitch drop), escape = rising arpeggio C-E-G-C. Length 30 s at 60 fps.
Description: Hard, soft or full jelly – which ball escapes the spinning ring first? 😳 Comment your pick before it ends!
Hashtags: #shorts #satisfying #softbody #physics #simulation
Tags: soft body simulation, 0% vs 100%, jelly ball, satisfying simulation, ball escape, spinning ring, physics simulation, oddly satisfying, bounce theory, which one wins

ideas.title: Spiral Chain Reaction (every wall hit splits)
ideas.hook: Frame 1: a single glowing white ball already rolling into the open mouth of a slowly rotating glowing spiral track.
ideas.why: GreyHaT Sim's 'Bouncing Emoji Balls Multiply in a Spiral!' has 3.95M views (12.6x). Your plain multiply Short ('1 ball becomes 200') got 2 views, so the multiply mechanic needs a new arena; the spiral gives it a visible goal (reach the centre).
ideas.script:
New sims.py function spiral_chain(). Arena: Archimedean spiral wall (r = 60 + 34·θ, 4.5 turns, line width 6) centred at (540, 900), rotating 0.35 rad/s; a glowing core circle r=45 at the centre. Start with 1 ball (r=14). Rule: every time a ball hits the spiral wall it splits into 2 (child gets ±15° velocity jitter), capped at 999 balls; ball radius shrinks from 14 to 6 as count grows. Gravity off; balls get a constant inward pull of 60 px/s² so they creep toward the core. Each ball's hue = its generation (rainbow cycle). Counter top-centre counts up. Win: first ball that touches the core triggers the core to flash and absorb all balls in a 2 s vacuum swirl. Looping ending: after the swirl, one white ball pops out of the core and flies back to the spiral mouth (= frame 1). On-screen lines (y=140-320): white 'Every hit = 2 balls', yellow 'Can 1 reach the centre? 🌀'; counter '1 → 999' at y≈1420. Sound: each split plays the next note of 'Ode to Joy' (public domain, synthesized bell timbre, max 12 notes/sec, gain rises with count); core hit = deep boom + whoosh. Background #06060b, spiral glow electric blue #3a7bff.
Description: One ball, a spinning spiral, and every hit doubles it. Does one make it to the centre? 🌀
Hashtags: #shorts #satisfying #chainreaction #simulation #physics
Tags: spiral simulation, chain reaction, balls multiply, every bounce 2 balls, satisfying simulation, physics simulation, 999 balls, oddly satisfying, bounce theory, rotating spiral

ideas.title: Complete the Ayah (3-option quiz)
ideas.hook: Frame 1: calm starry-sky loop with the first half of a famous ayah already on screen and three answer cards sliding in.
ideas.why: Question-led Islamic titles are outperforming (Tartil Offical's 'The Question That Leaves Every Soul Silent', 4.3x). Your quiz-style Shorts get started but your reminders are near 0 views; a fill-in-the-blank quiz gives a reason to stay to the reveal.
ideas.script:
Background: AE-starry-sky-01.mp4 (portrait, loop with 1 s cross-fade) or AE-foggy-forest-01.mp4, darkened 35%. Layout: line 1 (white, y=180): 'Complete the ayah 🤲'; line 2 (yellow, y=320): 'Only 1% get it right'. Main text (white, y=560-900): first half of the ayah in English. Three cards (y=1000-1400): A/B/C. 0-3 s question appears; 3-13 s 10-second countdown ring with soft tick (synthesized); 13 s correct card turns green with the full ayah and reference; 17-20 s 'Comment if you got it ✅'. Audio: soft pad drone + rain (synthesized), optional neutral AI voice reading the English only. NEVER a reciter recording. Today's two verified items (Sahih International wording): (1) 'Verily, in the remembrance of Allah…' A) do hearts find rest ✅ B) is wealth found C) are sins hidden — Ar-Ra'd 13:28. (2) 'For indeed, with hardship…' A) comes patience B) will be ease ✅ C) is reward — Ash-Sharh 94:5 (repeated in 94:6). Spare items for later days: 'Allah does not burden a soul…' → 'beyond that it can bear' (Al-Baqarah 2:286); 'So remember Me…' → 'I will remember you' (Al-Baqarah 2:152); 'And whoever relies upon Allah…' → 'then He is sufficient for him' (At-Talaq 65:3).
Description: Can you complete this ayah before the timer runs out? Comment your answer 🤲
Hashtags: #shorts #quran #islam #quiz #muslim

review.summary: Bounce Theory keeps growing (127.6K views in 28 days, +99 subs): brick breaker (9.5K, then 5.9K in 2 days), pendulum wave (31.9K and 8.0K) and string art (9.2K, 28 subs) are 6-8x your 1.2K median, and yesterday's remixes are already at 0.8-1.8K in under a day. Ambient Escape (29.3K views, +65 subs) still wins with verse reminders (median 1,173, 99% watched) and 'What Allah says about…' (1,092), but its last two days of Shorts mostly sit at 8-220 views while one salah line ('The version of you that prays on time wins') hit 1,045 in a day. Longs on both channels are still at 0-147 views; I can't watch the videos, so hook reads come from titles and the planned formats.
